assessment.nobel_worthiness: Elucidation of GLP-1 as an incretin and its conversion into durable receptor-agonist drugs is a rare complete arc from physiology to transformative therapy for type 2 diabetes and obesity. Importance is very high and the discovery is original and clear; clinical impact on cardiometabolic outcomes is large and still widening.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 biology and actions, GLP-2), Holst (physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action) and Knudsen (long-acting acylated analogues, liraglutide/semaglutide) form a coherent three-person configuration spanning basic and translational contributions. Mojsov's sequence and early peptide work is a real credit question that cannot be fully accommodated within three names.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism and clinical efficacy have been confirmed independently and at scale across multiple trials and drug classes; recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Fair treatment of Mojsov (and other early peptide-biochemistry contributors not on this list) is unresolved.
Relative weight of basic physiology versus industrial drug development is a judgment call from my recollection, not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering patients' T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality. The concept is original, the clinical proof is decisive and the field has extended to lupus and other autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (second-generation CD28 CAR design) and June (4-1BB CAR and first clinical successes in CLL/ALL) are the clearest decisive contributors; Rosenberg's earlier adoptive T-cell and gene-modified lymphocyte work is foundational but is a distinct line, and the credit to Eshhar and others outside this list is a known limitation.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long-term remission data from independent centres make the effect firmly established; recognition would be timely, though toxicity and solid-tumour limits remain.
uncertainties: Whether Rosenberg's contribution is core to CAR-T or belongs to a separate adoptive-therapy prize.
Absence of Zelig Eshhar from the credited names limits a fully fair allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a way to causally control defined cell populations with millisecond precision, transforming circuit analysis and underlying clinical efforts such as vision restoration. Originality and lasting methodological impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin identification and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) plus the neuronal implementation and broad application (Deisseroth, Boyden) are both decisive; with six credited names a three-person prize necessarily leaves out major contributors such as Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and independently replicated across thousands of labs; recognition is timely. Clinical translation is only beginning, which is acceptable for a tool prize.
uncertainties: Genuinely contested allocation among six credited people; the choice of three is not clearly resolvable from the supplied credit.
Whether a methods/tool discovery fits the physiology-or-medicine prize framing as well as a disease-oriented one.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery that cytosolic DNA is sensed by cGAS, producing cGAMP that activates STING, defined a central innate-immune pathway with relevance to infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies, cancer immunity and ageing. The mechanism is clear and mechanistically complete.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide second messenger cGAMP; Barber discovered STING and its role in DNA-triggered interferon induction. Together they cover the pathway's two key components; Ishikawa (STING co-discovery), Wu and Sun are junior or overlapping credits.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is robustly confirmed by many labs; therapeutic exploitation (STING agonists, inhibitors) is still early and not yet clinically validated, so recognition rests on basic-science impact.
uncertainties: Overlap of Barber's STING work with Ishikawa and others and priority details are not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response, including the Ire1-Hac1/XBP1 signalling mechanism and unconventional mRNA splicing, revealed how cells monitor and adapt to protein-folding stress, with broad implications for secretory-cell physiology, neurodegeneration, diabetes and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori made the decisive, complementary discoveries (Ire1 and its splicing role; Hac1/transcriptional response and the mammalian ATF6 pathway); a two-person configuration is clean and well defined, although other contributors (e.g. Ron on PERK/eIF2 arm, Kaufman) are not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Long-established, extensively confirmed concepts; timely to long-standing. Disease-therapeutic validation is still modest.
uncertainties: Omission of the PERK/integrated-stress-response arm in the credited names may leave the prize incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and its role as a central controller of cell growth and metabolism is a foundational discovery with major relevance to cancer, ageing, immunosuppression and metabolic disease.
assessment.attribution: Hall's genetic discovery of TOR and its function in growth control is the central contribution; Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin binding and target-oriented chemical biology is a prior, complementary step. Sabatini's later mTORC1 nutrient-sensing work is important but I would be cautious about including him without clearer attribution.
assessment.maturity: Pathway is very well confirmed and rapalogs are in clinical use; recognition is mature, and some dispute remains over how credit divides between pharmacology and genetics.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Schreiber and Sabatini is uncertain and I have not verified the details of earlier rapamycin-target work by others.
Therapeutic benefit of rapalogs is narrower than the pathway's biological importance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotide therapy for SMA (nusinersen) converted a lethal infant disease into a treatable one and validated antisense splicing modulation as a drug modality. Clarity of mechanism and clinical impact are strong.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the SMN2 exon 7 splicing mechanism and antisense targeting strategy; Bennett led the oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development at Ionis. This is a natural two-person pairing, though other academic and industry contributors exist.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with several years of real-world outcomes; independent confirmation is good, though the time since approval is moderate and the modality's generalizability is still being shown.
uncertainties: Relative contribution of target discovery versus oligonucleotide chemistry, and of others not credited, is not fully verifiable here.
Possible overlap with other nucleic-acid medicine recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle for membraneless compartments reframed cell biology and has stimulated work across development, neurodegeneration and cancer. The concept is original and widely influential.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman demonstrated liquid-like P granules and phase-separation-based organization; Gorlich and McKnight contributed related low-complexity-domain and nuclear-pore findings, but the decisive attribution is best captured in the Hyman-Brangwynne pair.
assessment.maturity: Maturity is the main concern: the physiological relevance and the precise meaning of 'condensate' are still debated, and in vivo evidence is uneven, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Debate over physiological relevance and over distinguishing phase separation from other assembly mechanisms.
Allocation among four credited names is unsettled and limited clinical translation to date.
